title: Astrid and the Harbor
premise: In the autumn of 1918, Zephyrine Whitlock arrives in the fog-bound port city of Astrid's Harbor to repair the observatory's failing master clock, carrying a sealed letter she was told never to open. When the clock's hidden compartment yields a second letter — naming her own family as keepers of a wartime promise to a German-born shipwright now branded an enemy — she must choose between the guild's silence and her conscience. As armistice negotiations stall and the harbor boils with suspicion, Zephyrine races to honor a promise made in peacetime, discovering that inheritance is not what we are given but what we choose to carry. The book ends with the clock striking the hour of the armistice, the promise fulfilled at cost, and Zephyrine claiming the harbor — and her family's true legacy — as her own.
about_author: Emrys Marchetti is the pen name of a former marine conservator who spent a decade restoring coastal lighthouses and clock towers along the North Atlantic. Their fiction explores how ordinary tradespeople become the quiet custodians of history.

chapters.title: The Hour That Stopped
chapters.summary: Zephyrine arrives in Astrid's Harbor, summoned by the guild to repair the observatory's master clock, which stopped at the exact minute war was declared. Through her POV, we feel her outsider's detachment — history is something that happens to other people. The beat is cautious wonder: a stranger in a town that watches her too closely.

chapters.title: A Letter, Sealed
chapters.summary: While cleaning the clock's works, Zephyrine finds a sealed letter tucked behind the escapement, addressed to 'the Whitlock who comes after.' Her POV. She is tempted, afraid, and strangely seen by the handwriting. The beat is the first crack in her belief that her family's story is small and unimportant.

chapters.title: The Shipwright's Bench
chapters.summary: Zephyrine traces the letter's references to a shuttered boatyard and meets Odile Vasseur, the yard's last keeper, who remembers a German-born shipwright named Anselm Krieg who vanished in 1914. Odile's POV. The beat is grief braided with warmth — two keepers of half a memory finding each other.

chapters.title: What the Guild Knows
chapters.summary: The guildmaster, Corvus Hale, warns Zephyrine to repair the clock and ask nothing, revealing that the letter concerns a promise made before the war: safe passage for Anselm's daughter, hidden somewhere in the harbor. Zephyrine's POV. The beat is dread — her family's name sits inside a plot everyone wants buried.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Bell Loft
chapters.summary: Following a child's chalk marks, Zephyrine discovers Lene, Anselm's daughter, living secretly in the observatory's bell loft, raised on the clockmaker's old kindness. Lene's POV. The beat is fragile hope — the promise is real, and it has been breathing quietly all along.

chapters.title: Armistice, Postponed
chapters.summary: News spreads that the armistice talks have stalled, and the harbor turns on anything German. Hale demands Lene be surrendered to the authorities; Odile refuses; Zephyrine's sealed letter is stolen. Zephyrine's POV. The beat is rising panic as private history collides with public fury.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Promise
chapters.summary: Zephyrine finally opens the sealed letter and learns her grandmother made the promise herself — safe passage, at any cost — and paid for it with exile. Zephyrine's POV, intercut with the grandmother's letter in her own voice. The beat is inheritance redefined: she is the promise now.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Harbor
chapters.summary: With the mob closing in, Zephyrine, Odile, and Lene attempt the escape by boat during a gale, while Hale, torn, chooses to delay the authorities rather than betray them. Alternating POVs. The beat is terror and resolve — the promise tested against the sea and the crowd.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Hour
chapters.summary: The boat founders; Zephyrine and Lene shelter in the observatory as the repaired master clock, wound by Odile's sacrifice, counts toward the armistice hour. Hale arrives — not with soldiers, but with papers declaring Lene a ward of the guild. Zephyrine's POV. The climax: the promise kept as the clock strikes eleven.

chapters.title: What the Clock Keeps
chapters.summary: Weeks after the armistice, Zephyrine is offered the observatory post and Lene's guardianship; the town, slowly, begins to remember Anselm's name with honor instead of suspicion. Zephyrine's POV. The beat is quiet belonging — she winds the clock, opens the workshop, and finally calls the harbor home.
